Bobby Moore Academy
We celebrate the diversity of our community through our aspirational learning culture so that each individual can fulfil their potential.
Our Academy
Vision and Values
Our vision is that the education we provide to our pupils is both empowering and engaging. We believe firmly that every pupil at Bobby Moore Academy has a right to a world class education, and that the end goal of education should be to furnish pupils with choice. This belief is founded upon education being a 'Master Key' and an absolute conviction that each of our pupils has the capacity to become knowledgeable, articulate, compassionate and industrious young people. We are committed to the communities we serve, and encourage our pupils to think of themselves as future leaders within these communities.
Our mission is clear, based in a foundation of core values, and we believe every member of our Academy community can say;
We are the drivers of social mobility.
We address social injustice head on.
We are architects of aspirations.
We are unrelenting in our focus on academic achievement.
Our expectations are uncompromising.
We craft good character.
We are custodians of the ‘master key’.

The David Ross Education Trust

Bobby Moore Academy
We celebrate the diversity of our community through our aspirational learning culture so that each individual can fulfil their potential.
Principal's Welcome
Sarah Donnelly, Principal
Welcome to Bobby Moore Academy. My name is Sarah Donnelly and, as Principal, I would like to welcome you to the Bobby Moore Academy Website where you can read about our Primary phase, Secondary phase and Sixth Form provision.
We are a thriving, ambitious, and welcoming school community that delivers a world-class education for boys and girls in East London. Our modern and spacious Primary and Secondary sites are next to the London Stadium in the beautiful Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park. Following the examples set by the London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games and Bobby Moore as World Cup-winning captain in 1966, we value hard work and dedication, ambition and leadership, alongside respect and integrity. We firmly believe that by installing the importance of Physical, Mental and Social Wellbeing, our students will become economically active and fulfilled citizens, that lead enjoyable, healthy and active lifestyles throughout their adulthood.
Background does not determine destiny.
At the heart of this success is an absolute belief in the ability of every student to shine – no matter what their background, ability or character. We combine the traditional values of discipline, respect and good behaviour with contemporary best practice in teaching, learning and technology.
We will accept no excuses for being anything but the best we can be. We focus on the development of our students as individuals, and guide them by allowing honest, trusting and equal relationships to form. We do this by regularly monitoring progress and understanding, using our developmental marking policy, class discussion, and role-modelling of expected behaviours.
Children learn best when their school environment is safe, inclusive and welcoming. We have a culture of mutual respect between students and staff, and zero tolerance of bullying in any form.
The best from every child.
We will work hard to get the best from all our students, reinforced by very clear expectations regarding conduct, manners, uniform and behavior which are non-negotiable and consistently enforced across the academy. We believe that success occurs in a framework of high expectations, whilst also acknowledging that mistakes provide valuable learning opportunities too.
When a student joins our academy some will already be high-fliers, others will be good all-rounders and some will face significant and individual challenges. Each student will already have a unique personality, gift and character that we will develop further by working together. I have made it clear to everyone at the academy that we are stronger as a team than a group of individuals, and that by pulling in the same direction we will achieve great things.
As part of the David Ross Education Trust, we are at the leading edge of education in the UK. As a student at Bobby Moore Academy opportunities are made available from the Trust that enable them to take part in once in a lifetime activities and learning experiences. Like our students, our staff are constantly looking to improve and hone their practice which they do by accessing the wealth of support of the whole Trust of schools and not just BMA.
By providing an excellent education for every step of a child’s journey from age 4 through to 18, we will equip them with the knowledge and attributes to succeed throughout their time at school, and beyond it as well-rounded members of our community. Ultimately, our goal is that regardless of circumstances, every young person should be empowered through education to choose and succeed on their own path in life.
We believe that every member of our community can confidently say;
We are the drivers of social mobility.
We address social injustice head on.
We are architects of aspirations.
We are unrelenting in our focus on academic achievement.
Our expectations are uncompromising.
We craft good character.
We are custodians of the ‘master key’.
Thank you for taking an interest in our academy. Whether you are a parent, prospective parent or member of our wider community, please feel free to contact us if there is anything further you require.
Principal (All Through)

Our Governors
Bobby Moore Academy is governed by an Academy Scrutiny Committee.
Our governors are:
Sarah Donnelly
Kirstie Kershaw
Kirstie was drawn to Bobby Moore Academy by it's vision and values to empower children to become whatever their dreams desire, starting at reception and reaching beyond. Kirstie has worked at Bobby Moore Academy since 2018, beginning as a 1-1, each year moving onto a larger role, TA, HLTA and more recently as a teacher.
Some of the key attributes Kirstie brings to the table include my enthusiasm for learning and personal growth, a forward thinking, creative approach to crafting long-term relationships with children and adults alike, and a fun approach to boost pupil engagement.
Kirstie is passionate about reading, and her vivid imagination helps her visualise the books she reads.
Oliver Speakman
As he was looking to develop his own understanding of the 'hidden' side of running a school Oliver joined the ASC in September 2025. Oliver is one of the longest serving members of staff at Bobby Moore Academy and knows the scholars well. In his paid role, Oliver is Head of Maths but has previously served as Head of Year and Lead Practitioner.
Outside of Bobby Moore, Oliver is an avid puzzler, especially when it comes to sudokus and crosswords. Oliver also loves cooking and learning new dishes from cuisines across the world.
Juliet Jaggs
Juliet spent twenty years as a teacher and senior leader in secondary schools, where she fulfilled academic and pastoral roles including those associated with inclusion, sixth form and boarding.
Lorimer Tucker
Larry was born just over 2 miles away from Bobby Moore Academy and spent his entire working life in the Lloyd's Insurance market in the City of London. Educated at Forest School in Snaresbrook, he became a Partner in his firm in 1988 and a Chartered Insurer upon its launch in 1996. During his work career, he specialised in problem solving and innovation, which, before his retirement in 2015, included industry presentations and the mentoring of others.
Leonard Alexander
Lenny joined the ASC in November 2023. He is an Insurance Consultant for several Global insurance brokers institutions and leads teams negotiating terms and insurance claims values on behalf of International Commercial customers. His passions include Photography, travel, family, reading.
Kareena Begum
Kareena has been teaching for over 15 years in Social Sciences and Healthcare. She has taught in inner London schools and sixth form colleges and has lead teams and departments. She has experience in engaging with her local community, doing volunteer work and supporting people and organisations.
Mala Narula
As she was looking to grow personally and professionally in a way that allowed her to give back to her community, Mala joined the Bobby Moore Academy ASC in November 2025.
Mala works as a Senior Internal Audit Manager for a FTSE 50 Distribution organisation. Her role focusses on assessing risks within the business through gaining a good understanding of processes. Mala provides recommendations to business for operational efficiency, process improvement and risk management.
Outside of work Mala enjoys travel, cricket, coaching and mentoring and Zumba dancing.
Paul Jackson
Impressed with both the philosophy and results of The David Ross Education Trust, Paul hoped his 40 years of experience within education could add to the work of the Trust. He became a Governor in February 2026.
Outside of education, Paul carries out charity work with Round Table, Rotary and 41 Club. Paul also volunteers at Northampton General Hospital and St Andrews Mental Health organisation. Paul also enjoys British History, Squash, Golf and Padel.
Quraisha Rawat
As she values quality and is passionate about developing and enabling others Quraisha came to the Governor role in March 2026. Being a Governor provides Quraisha with the opportunity to use her 20+ years experience in professional services to give back to her community.
In her paid role Quraisha is a Chartered Accountant, working within Audit & Assurance at Deloitte.
Outside of work Quraisha loves nature and walks in the countryside and woods. Quraisha also enjoys travelling and experiencing new places and cultures. A keen sports fan, Quraisha is emotionally invested in football, rugby, cricket and formula one.
Preslav Tonkov
Preslav Tonkov is a strategic adviser to global organizations focused on quantifying and improving worldwide human development issues. As a Senior Advisor at Gallup, he supports a global research portfolio that bridges evidence gaps for decision-makers at the World Bank, WHO, and various UN agencies. Having been educated within the Newham school system, Preslav brings a local perspective alongside an International Relations degree and a Master's degree in Social Research, both from the London School of Economics. He specializes in translating complex data into actionable insights, drawing on extensive experience at international policy forums such as the UN World Data Forum and the World Health Summit to address critical developmental challenges.
Lidia Jung
Lidia believes that all children should have access to the best education and wanted to play a part in an Academy that strives to deliver it. Lidia has a keen interest in the unique opportunities that the Academy has to offer scholars due to the location and proximity to the many educational, sporting and creative organisations and how to make the most of those links for the benefit of the scholars.
In her work, Lidia is the Founder and Director of an Interior Design studio, Visiting Lecturer at the London College of Fashion, University of the Arts, Lecturer in Fashion Accessories and also delivers design theory workshops. Lidia has a background in product design and was a Senior Designer of leather goods and accessories for luxury brands for over a decade.
Outside of work Lidia enjoys visiting galleries and the theatre with her family.
Dawud Marsh
Looking to share his education and governance expertise, Dawud joined the ASC in July 2025.
In his paid employment, Dawud is a co-director of ICM Foundation CIC and co-coordinates a project supporting adults with learning difficulties and disabilities.
Outside of work, Dawud enjoys amateur photography, fine art, creative writing, running, activities in the outdoors with his family and cooking vegan food.

Contacting Us
The Governance Officer for Bobby Moore Academy is Victoria Linthwaite. Victoria can be reached at governance@dret.co.uk.
To contact a governor, please contact the Trust Governance Team by emailing governance@dret.co.uk.
If you are looking to contact a Governor to make a complaint or share a concern, please note that as per our Complaints Policy, governors do not investigate complaints at Stage 1 or Stage 2. This enables them to be impartial should a complaint be escalated to a Stage 3 governor panel. If you wish to make a complaint, please complete this form and your complaint will be investigated accordingly.
Scheme of Delegation
Information about the David Ross Education Trust's scheme of delegation is available here.
Minutes of the Academy Scrutiny Committee
Should you wish to view a copy of the minutes of the ASC at this academy, please contact the Trust Governance Team (governance@dret.co.uk), who will be able to provide you with an electronic or paper copy of the minutes.
Are you interested in becoming an academy governor?
We are looking for new governors to support our academies. Our governors work closely with their academies to support the Trust’s goal of broadening the horizons of young people through a world-class education, equipping our students with the skills and experiences to become their confident, academic best, no matter what.
If you have an interest in, and commitment to, improving education and would like to make a difference within your community, please register your interest in becoming a governor by completing our governor application form. If you have any questions about a governor’s role or responsibilities please contact us at governance@dret.co.uk or review our information pack below.
aug 2025 governor recruitment booklet.pdf
What is it like being a Governor with DRET?
To understand what it is like to be a governor with us, take a look at our main Trust page which features a testimonial booklet and videos which contain insights from serving governors.
What training to Governors receive?
We offer an extensive range of training opportunities. Take a look at what is on offer for the current academic year.

Bobby Moore Academy is a school that understands the paramount significance of building partnerships and social networks with providers in varying fields.
Our commitment to forging alliances with esteemed organisations such as London Youth Rowing, EastEd, West Ham FC, UCL, British Cycling, BBC Singers, The Royal Drawing School, Bath Festival Orchestra, and LLDC has allowed us to ignite a spark of opportunity for our students and enhance social mobility in the vibrant borough of Newham.
Partnerships are the cornerstones of progress and success. They have the incredible power to unlock doors that may otherwise remain closed and open uncharted avenues of growth. At Bobby Moore Academy, we recognise that no single entity can cater to the holistic development of our students. We believe in collaboration and synergy; harnessing the unique strengths of our partners to create an enriched learning environment.
Take the partnership with London Youth Rowing: In joining forces, we have not only introduced our students to the wonders of rowing but also instilled in them a deep sense of discipline, teamwork, and resilience. Similarly, our partnership with EastEd ensures that our students have access to a network of individuals committed to transforming the educational experience.
Whether through scientific research, artistic expression, or community engagement, we empower students to embrace the world. The importance of building social networks cannot be overstated. By collaborating with providers in varying fields, we create a web of support and opportunity for our students, ensuring that their dreams are not confined by circumstance, but rather nurtured and expanded upon. Partnerships allow us to bring expertise, and perspectives into our classrooms.
The fruits of our partnerships extend beyond the confines of the academy. Our commitment to improving social mobility in Newham is the heart that beats within us: let us celebrate the power of partnership and the beautiful dance it weaves between education and opportunity. Together we are writing a story of triumph, where our students become the authors of their own destiny. In fostering these connections, we are creating a legacy of social mobility that ripples through Newham, empowering generations to come.

PSHE and RSE and RE at BMA
Daily year group character time sessions, whole school assemblies and timetabled PSHE periods are used to address significant topical issues and place prominence on our school values. Religious Education (RE) is covered as a discrete subject at Key Stage 3 and as part of the broader PSHE and assembly programme for Key Stage 4 and 5. Religious Education is a whole cohort subject at GCSE level and remains an option as an A-level subject for all students in Key Stage 5. Relationships, Sex and Health (RSE) education is also covered within tutor time and drop-down days across the academic year. This curriculum covers all recommended content for personal, social, health and economic education (PSHE).
If you have further questions for enquiries regarding the KS3 or KS4 curriculum, please contact Mr Bonthron using the BMA contact us email.
Our approach to the curriculum complies with our equality objectives and pays due regard to the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014. We work to the best of our ability to ensure that all barriers are lifted for all students, so that they can achieve their potential and access to the curriculum. We encourage all to not only take a full and active part in lessons but also ensure all students have equal opportunity to participate in our enrichment opportunities.
